name: Waddell
title: Waddell, AZ real estate: acreage, new builds and the White Tanks
seoTitle: Waddell AZ Homes, Acreage and Land | Teigh Wade REALTOR®
description: Waddell is unincorporated Maricopa County near Loop 303 and the White Tanks. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, explains acreage, wells, septic, HOAs and new subdivisions.
summary: Waddell is an unincorporated community in Maricopa County, west of Glendale and south of Surprise, with the 85355 ZIP code. It mixes rural acreage, some with horse privileges, private water and septic, with newer HOA subdivisions near Loop 303 and the White Tank Mountains. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, lives next door in Surprise.

sections.h2: Where Waddell is, and what unincorporated means
sections.html:
Waddell is not a city. It is an unincorporated community in Maricopa County, which means there is no Waddell city hall, no city council and no city building department. County agencies handle zoning, permits and road maintenance, and services such as water and trash often come from private companies instead of a municipality. Some streets near Waddell have been annexed by neighboring cities over the years, so a home with a Waddell mailing address can sit in county land or inside Glendale or Surprise. Checking the jurisdiction is step one.

The community carries the name of Donald Ware Waddell, an investor whose firm financed the dam that first created Lake Pleasant. He laid out a small townsite in 1935 at Waddell Road and Cotton Lane, and a post office followed in 1937. The town itself never fully developed, but the name stuck. The current post office, built in 1992, sits near Glendale Avenue and Cotton Lane, and the ZIP code is 85355.

Teigh Wade lives a few minutes away in Surprise, so Waddell is part of her everyday territory, not a place she drives out to once a year.

Rural lots and acreage

A large part of Waddell is still rural. Clearwater Farms, for example, is known for parcels of roughly one to three acres where animals are allowed. Listings in these areas often show features you rarely see in a city subdivision: corrals, stalls, tack rooms, arenas, flood irrigation, a private water company or a well, and a septic tank instead of a sewer line. Homes range from older manufactured and site-built houses to custom homes on acreage.

Newer subdivisions

The other side of Waddell is newer master-planned and builder communities, mostly built from the 2000s to today. Names buyers see include Cortessa, which has greenbelts and mountain-view paths, Granite Vista, Windrose (part of the Zanjero Trails master plan), Zanjero Pass, and White Tank Foothills. These neighborhoods look much like those in Surprise or Goodyear: stucco and tile roofs, two-car or three-car garages, one- and two-story plans, community parks and an HOA.

sections.h2: Due diligence on rural Waddell homes
sections.html:
Rural property rewards careful questions. Teigh helps buyers line these up during the inspection period:

  1. Water source. Is the home on a private water company, a shared well or its own private well? For a well, ask for the well registration, pump age, and a water quality and flow test.
  2. Septic system. Arizona requires a septic inspection when a home on a conventional septic system transfers. Find out the tank size, its age and when it was last pumped.
  3. Irrigation. Some acreage is flood irrigated. Ask who delivers the water, how the schedule works, what the assessments are and whether the irrigation rights convey with the land.
  4. Horse privileges and zoning. Do not assume animals are allowed. Confirm the county zoning and any deed restrictions, and look at fencing, shade structures and arena footing.
  5. Road access and utilities. Some roads are unpaved or privately maintained. Ask who maintains the road, and confirm the electric provider and internet options for the parcel.
  6. Manufactured homes. If a home is manufactured, check that it is permanently affixed and properly titled, since that affects financing.

Buyers in the newer subdivisions have a different list: HOA documents and dues, any leased solar panels, pool inspections, and whether the builder warranty transfers. Teigh's home buying help covers both.

The White Tank Mountains rise along the western edge of the area. White Tank Mountain Regional Park, managed by Maricopa County Parks and Recreation, is the largest regional park in the county, and Waddell is the nearest community to it. The park has close to 26 miles of trails, many open to biking and horseback riding, and the popular Waterfall Trail leads to a canyon with a seasonal waterfall and Hohokam petroglyphs along the way.

Nearby attractions also include Wildlife World Zoo and several golf courses on the Surprise and Glendale side. The White Tank Regional Library, a county branch, opened in 2010.

Loop 303 is the big change for Waddell. It follows the Cotton Lane corridor through the area and connects south to I-10 in Goodyear and north to Surprise, Peoria and I-17. Major arterials include Northern Avenue, Glendale Avenue, Olive Avenue, Cactus Road, Waddell Road and Cotton Lane, while US-60 (Grand Avenue) lies a few miles to the northeast. Distances between homes can be long, so map your regular trips before you choose a parcel.

Because Waddell spans a wide area, school assignments depend on the exact parcel. Parts of Waddell are served by Dysart Unified School District, and other parts by Litchfield Elementary School District and Agua Fria Union High School District. Confirm the assigned schools with the district for any property.

Electric service comes from APS in much of the West Valley, but confirm the provider for any parcel, along with water, trash and internet. Fire and law enforcement for unincorporated areas are handled by county and regional agencies rather than a city department.

Waddell buyers ask very specific questions, and a listing that answers them up front stands out. Expect to be asked about the well or water company, the septic system, irrigation rights, horse setup, lot size, fencing, road access, solar and whether there is an HOA. For rural homes, gathering well records, septic paperwork and irrigation details before you list can prevent delays later.

Photos matter too. Acreage, barns and mountain views need wide, well-lit shots, and the inside of the home should look as cared for as the outside. Teigh's listing clients get staging help as part of her service; see the home staging page for the options. Rural values depend heavily on the land, water and improvements, so Teigh prepares a comparative market analysis rather than quoting area averages, and she never guarantees a price.

Teigh Wade is a REALTOR® with HomeSmart Elite Group, HomeSmart. She is an Arizona native who has lived mostly in the West Valley, and Waddell is right down the road from her home in Surprise.

faqs.a: No. Waddell is an unincorporated community in Maricopa County, so the county handles zoning, permits and roads instead of a city government. Some nearby streets have been annexed by Glendale or Surprise, which means a Waddell mailing address does not always mean county land. Check the jurisdiction for each property you are considering.

Waddell uses the 85355 ZIP code, with a post office near Glendale Avenue and Cotton Lane. Because ZIP codes follow postal routes rather than city limits, some 85355 homes fall in unincorporated county land and others fall inside a neighboring city. The parcel record from the county assessor shows the jurisdiction.

faqs.q: Are there horse properties in Waddell?
faqs.a: Yes, in parts of Waddell. Rural areas such as Clearwater Farms have parcels of roughly one to three acres, and some listings include horse privileges, corrals, stalls and arenas. Never assume animals are allowed on a specific lot. Confirm the zoning and any deed restrictions, and inspect the fencing and facilities before you buy.

faqs.q: Do Waddell homes have wells and septic systems?
faqs.a: Many rural homes do. Some acreage properties use a private water company or a private well and a septic tank instead of city water and sewer. Newer subdivisions are usually connected to a water provider and sewer. For any home on septic, Arizona requires an inspection at transfer, and buyers should ask for well records and water testing.

faqs.q: Do newer Waddell subdivisions have HOAs?
faqs.a: Yes. Communities such as Cortessa, Granite Vista, Windrose and Zanjero Pass are builder or master-planned neighborhoods with homeowner associations, common areas and parks. Rural acreage is less likely to have an HOA, though some parcels have deed restrictions. Teigh reviews the HOA or deed documents with buyers before the inspection period ends.

faqs.q: How close is Waddell to the White Tank Mountains?
faqs.a: Very close. Waddell is the nearest community to White Tank Mountain Regional Park, the largest regional park in Maricopa County. The park has close to 26 miles of trails for hiking, biking and horseback riding, plus the Waterfall Trail and Hohokam petroglyphs.

faqs.q: What freeway is closest to Waddell?
faqs.a: Loop 303 runs through the area along the Cotton Lane corridor. It reaches I-10 to the south in Goodyear and continues north toward Surprise, Peoria and I-17. US-60 (Grand Avenue) is a few miles northeast. Northern Avenue, Glendale Avenue and Olive Avenue are the main east-west routes toward Glendale and Phoenix.

It depends on the parcel. Parts of Waddell fall in Dysart Unified School District, and other parts are served by Litchfield Elementary School District and Agua Fria Union High School District. School boundaries can change, so confirm the assigned schools directly with the district before you choose a home.
